summary.scope: Seven published external versions from existing proof; six government contributors excluded from external cohort. Unpublished or other-channel completeness not claimed.
limits: Scope is seven previously archived external KLtgV responses,35authorpages; unpublished/other-channel responses and six government contributors are outside the pilot.
Assessments cover inventoried potentially material claims and interpretive premises. They do not certify every assertion or establish a representative error rate.
Supported means the bounded proposition is corroborated; unresolved means evidence, applicability, interpretation or quantification remains open.
Full paid standards and human specialist verification were not available. Current publisher descriptions and dated primary research establish only their explicit contents.
The archived draft is internally8July2026; byte identity with references to7July is not authenticated. Authored dates are not independently verified delivery dates.
Repeated reading adds zero units to the existing626-entry ledger.
conclusions: The final ledger contains111claim assessments:75supported,35unresolved and one narrow overstatement. All108initial assessments were independently peer-reviewed; three additional bounded premises were independently adjudicated by the lead reviewer.
One new provisional minor finding: transport pipelines do not cross state borders by definition. There is no new major finding, and the case for nationwide uniform rules remains.

Primary engineering evidence corroborates several uncited factual premises about phase behaviour, corrosion/impurities and running ductile fracture. Costs, detailed standard adequacy and several legal interpretations remain unresolved.

A proposed error concerning CCSnecessity was not admitted after independent review: the2022report’s selected-scenario conclusions and the2045versus2050distinction support a reasonable contextual reading.
This is deeper verification of the same seven submissions, not new document coverage or a national error-rate estimate.
